title: Sell Mineral Rights in Broadview, MT
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Broadview, MT
metaDescription: Broadview sits in northern Yellowstone County dryland farm country. A former engineer explains realistic mineral value away from the river irrigation belt.
heroLead: Broadview sits up on the dryland side of Yellowstone County, away from the irrigated valley floor, and that changes both the farming and the mineral history compared to towns closer to the river.
intro: Unlike Huntley or Ballantine down in the irrigated Yellowstone Valley, Broadview sits in the county's northern dryland wheat country, settled under standard homestead patents rather than a reclamation project. Mineral severance history here follows the more typical Montana pattern: severed at some point from the surface, carried through generations, and rarely tied to any current oil and gas development.

sections.heading: Dryland Homestead Title
paragraphs: Confirming your family's interest near Broadview usually means tracing a standard homestead patent through however many sales and inheritances happened over the last century. I check the recorded chain at the courthouse and compare it against whatever documentation the family has, since older transfers weren't always recorded promptly.

sections.heading: No Meaningful Drilling History
paragraphs: I'm not aware of any significant oil and gas development in the immediate Broadview area, and I check current permit records to confirm that before giving any value estimate. This part of Yellowstone County has stayed agricultural, without the kind of leasing interest that shows up closer to more active basins.

sections.heading: Setting a Fair Expectation
paragraphs: For a Broadview-area interest, I'd expect a modest, speculative value with no current income attached, and I say that plainly rather than build up expectations that a title check and permit search won't support.

That said, dryland tracts in this part of Yellowstone County occasionally sit near old exploratory holes drilled decades ago and never developed further. If your family's abstract mentions a test well or a dry hole from years back, I'd want to see that record too, since it can shed light on the formation depths beneath your specific section.

faqs.question: Is Broadview, MT near any active oil and gas development?
faqs.answer: Not that current permit records show. This is dryland farm country in northern Yellowstone County without significant drilling history.

faqs.question: How do I trace an old homestead patent near Broadview?
faqs.answer: Start at the Yellowstone County Clerk and Recorder in Billings for the recorded chain of title, and check the Bureau of Land Management's General Land Office records online for the original federal patent if needed.

faqs.question: Is it worth holding onto an undeveloped mineral interest near Broadview?
faqs.answer: That's a personal decision based on your own timeline. I'll give you an honest, modest value range reflecting the lack of current development, and you can weigh that against simply holding the interest.

faqs.question: What does an old abstract of title actually show?
faqs.answer: An abstract compiles every recorded document affecting a tract, deeds, leases, mortgages, and probate filings, in one chronological packet. For a Broadview-area interest, it's often the fastest way to spot an old test well or exploratory lease the current owner never knew about.
